title: Hubble Interacting Galaxy Mrk 273
caption: Merging galaxy Markarian 273, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Mrk 273, UGC 8696, I Zw 071 · constellation Ursa Major · about 500 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration, and A. Evans (University of Virginia, Charlottesville/NRAO/Stony Brook University)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Markarian 273 has a bizarre shape that NASA likens to a toothbrush. Hubble shows an intricate central region and a long tail running diagonally toward the lower right of the frame. That tail stretches about 130 thousand light-years and is strong evidence that two galaxies have merged here.

The galaxy has an intense starburst region, where new stars amounting to 60 times the mass of our Sun are born each year. Observations in near-infrared light, which passes more easily through dust, show that the nucleus has two separate components.

Seen in infrared light, Markarian 273 ranks among the most luminous galaxies known. It lies 500 million light-years from Earth in Ursa Major. The image is part of a collection of 59 merging and interacting galaxies released in April 2008 to mark the telescope's 18th launch anniversary.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took this image. NASA has not published which filters were used or how colors were assigned.
understand.eye: Markarian 273 is especially luminous in infrared light, which the eye cannot see, and the 37-minute exposure gathers far more light than the eye can.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration, and A. Evans (University of Virginia, Charlottesville/NRAO/Stony Brook University)

behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The galaxy is also cataloged as UGC 8696 and I Zw 071. According to NASA, astronomers study systems like this to learn how gravity steers colliding galaxies, and the 2008 set was meant to show collisions at many different stages.
alt: A galaxy with an intricate center and a long tail running diagonally toward the bottom right, resembling a toothbrush.
